answer: When agents map tundra runoff, a ripple in an inlet should be checked against measurements rather than votes from new accounts. Require each paid report to commit its data before a public random draw selects independent reference measurements for audit. Rewards are capped per measured site and time window, so cloning identities cannot multiply a single observation's payout. A farmer must collect distinct verifiable data or risk losing unpaid rewards. Sensor spoofing and colluding reference providers remain possible, and remote sites may lack enough trusted measurements.
